title: Starmer Moves to Nationalize British Steel
excerpt: UK PM announces legislation to bring Scunthorpe steelmaker into public ownership for first time since 1988
body:
Prime Minister Keir Starmer announced on Monday, May 11, that his Labour government will introduce legislation this week to take British Steel into full public ownership — ending months of uncertainty for the company, its workers, and its supply chain.

**What happened:**
Starmer declared that negotiations with British Steel's Chinese owner, Jingye, had made a commercial sale impossible, and that the public interest test for nationalization could now be met. The new Bill, set to appear in the King's Speech on Wednesday, would give the government power to take full national ownership of British Steel, subject to that public interest test — covering factors such as national security, critical infrastructure, and the broader economy. British Steel could return to government hands for the first time since being sold off in 1988.

**Why it matters:**
The government first intervened at British Steel in April 2025 under the Steel Industry (Special Measures) Act to ensure uninterrupted steel production and to avoid the sudden closure of the blast furnaces. The cost of supporting British Steel is set to reach 615 million pounds ($836 million) by June, according to the country's spending watchdog. UK Steel, the industry trade association, said the decision 'brings much-needed certainty for British Steel's skilled workforce and customers,' adding that steel 'remains essential to the UK's national security, infrastructure delivery and economic resilience.'

**What to watch:**
The new Bill will be formally introduced to Parliament this week, and any decision to bring British Steel into public ownership would only be taken after the Bill receives Royal Assent and the public interest test is met.
nri_angle: Indian-Americans in manufacturing, infrastructure, and finance should watch closely — a nationalized British Steel could reshape global steel supply chains and signal a broader Western shift toward industrial policy that echoes debates playing out in U.S. Congress right now.
